**Step 1 — Scene:** A breakfast plate with scrambled eggs, browned shredded potatoes, and a toasted bagel half with cream cheese. A little red sauce is visible on the eggs.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A square plate approximately 24 cm across, with an effective circular diameter of about 26 cm. Estimated area: 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Bagel half, cream cheese, hash browns, scrambled eggs, and red sauce. Cooking fat is included in the cooked-food energy estimates rather than counted separately.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:** Area shares below partition the visible food coverage; cream cheese is allocated separately from exposed bagel.

| Bagel half | 17% | 90 × 0.95 = 86 ml | 0.9 | 77 g | 270 | 208 kcal |
| Cream cheese | 8% | 42 × 0.35 = 15 ml | 1.0 | 15 g | 340 | 51 kcal |
| Hash browns | 22% | 117 × 1.3 = 152 ml | 0.65 | 99 g | 180 | 178 kcal |
| Scrambled eggs | 20% | 106 × 1.4 = 149 ml | 0.95 | 141 g | 160 | 226 kcal |
| Red sauce | 1% | 5.3 × 0.2 = 1 ml | 1.0 | 1 g | 50 | 1 kcal |

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Food covers approximately **68%** of the plate. The estimated **333 g and 664 kcal** are plausible for the visible eggs, potatoes, and generously topped bagel half. The largest uncertainties are bagel thickness and cooking fat.
